doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: New building and collections
summary: The move to a new building and collections including Ellison's records and Lockjaw Davis's saxophone.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We moved to a new building about 2-1/2 years ago and it’s spanking new and great. We just have a large one room, but we have some great collections. We have Ralph Ellison’s the recordings that he listened to when he was writing “Invisible Man.”

We have that. We have Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis’s tenor sax and I went out to his family’s house in Las Vegas, all his things. So his reeds and his matchbook covers from Birdland, and the album that his mother made when he was a kid. We have the Savory Collection which are unissued recordings going back to the 1930s and 40s. We have a handful of collections like that that are very very special.
